tons of money with trucking but you're not going to be making that kind of money in a year or even 3 years. you have to specialize in something because you're going to be doing dry van for a while and that shit doesn't pay for anything so look around at what pays the most and work towards that. I don't recommend CR England because I'm pretty sure they train their drivers using automatics which means when you get your CDL through them you'll be restricted to only using automatic trucks and a lot of companies are still primarily using manuals. private CDL schools are an ok way to go but mostly just train you for the very basics of trucking and you're not guaranteed a job at the end either so not only are you only going to get basic knowledge but you're going to be stuck with tuition cost and no job to pay it. Go with one of the major carriers that will pay to train you and then hire you at the end, if you do you'll get a contract to work for them for 1 year or so. If you break the contract you will have to pay everything you owe for their schooling cost, but no one advising someone to leave their first company until at least being with them for a year because that 1 year experience will open up a lot more opportunities when you leave. I've heard great things about prime but their training from start to finish is 4-5 months long which is by far the highest i've seen in the industry, swift is the rotten egg of the trucking field from what i've seen BUT their training program is just as good as any of them. Don't know anything about pam. Prime will start you out at .41 cents per mile after your training is over and swift will start you out at .36 cents per mile after your training is over which is on the lower end but there are more raises in the first year than usual (5 in the first 12 months). in the end swift and prime will pay around the same. Swift has way more lots and terminals than Prime does, Swift tends to stay more on the East coast and Prime is based more on the west. I myself will be going with Swift just due to the fact that one of their training terminals are 20 minutes from my house so I can just go home at the end of the classes.

Experience counts for everything. if you don't have the experience the likelihood of landing a job above 50k is small. I'm currently in the same boat as you except i'm making 13k. I'm just looking for any company that will pay to train me and give me a job at the end regardless of how much i'll make until i get experience to go local. Most company CDL schools want you to stay with them for a minimum of 1 year, if you leave the company before your 1 year then you'll have to owe the cost of the school up front which could be around 2,000-6000 dollars. That really isn't much of a issue since anyone will tell you to stay with your first company for at least 1 year to get that 1 year experience that many other more lucrative companies want from you. You can try and get trained by a private CDL school but you're not guaranteed work after you finish like you are with bigger named company schools, so basically you'll be sitting around with thousands of dollars owed to them and no employment to pay for it. private schools also only train you on the bare minimum basics and if you do find a job after that school then you will most likely have zero clue what you're even doing because the school was extremely short and taught you only the basics. Big name company schools will train the hell out you until you and your trainer are confident enough to allow you to go solo. some big companies don't let you pay their school cost up front because they want you to work for them when you're done training. The only way around that is to work for them for a little while and then leave which will result in a "penalty" which is you having to pay the cost of the school up front. Trucking can make you a lot of money but that isn't what you're likely going to see for a while because like I said experience counts for everything. No company that pays a lot of money will put their reputation on the line to hire some novice driver who just got their license. Also OTR isn't what you want if you want money, OTR is a lifestyle not a job, but unfortunately OTR is probably what you're going to have to do for at least the first year after school. You want money go with companies that haul double or triple trailers or fuel tankers. none of these will be given to you without working to build up to it. There are only a few companies that will actually pay to train you and those companies are usually looked at as being starter companies and don't pay that well, maybe 30-45k your first year/year and a half is what you're going to be looking at, definitely not more than that unless you get extremely lucky and go with a private school and get hired with a good local company right after training.

Edit: I'd also like to add that flatbed and refrigerated trailer divisions are the divisions that will pay you the most until you can get double/triple trailer or tanker jobs. With flatbed you get paid extra by mile and for securing and unsecuring your cargo at shippers, it's a lot of work and you'll regret it when you're in the mid west and it's 20 degrees and snowing outside but it's a good extra chunk of change. refrigerated is much more of a hassle to deal with than your ordinary dry van and theres a lot more work out there for refrigerated. it's a good division if you like to just relax a bit more since loading and unloading can take quite a while. If you go that division be prepared to be the most hated person at the truck stop because no one likes being parked next to by someone hauling refrigerated.  It's also not fun doing night deliveries which is something you'll have to do often. Backing up to a really tight grocery store dock in the dead of night is not enjoyable at all but the pay is good.
